name: Shapiro-Wilk normality test
hypothesis: H0: log(price_usd_per_tonne) across all mineral-year observations is normally distributed.
interpretation: Reject H0: log-transformed prices are not normally distributed (p<0.05), which is expected given the mix of very different minerals in the pool; this motivates using non-parametric tests below rather than assuming normality.

name: Mann-Whitney U test
hypothesis: H0: demand_growth_pct has the same distribution for rare-earth vs. non-rare-earth minerals.
interpretation: Fail to reject H0 (p=0.1318): no statistically significant difference in demand-growth distribution between rare-earth and non-rare-earth minerals in this dataset.

name: Kruskal-Wallis H test
hypothesis: H0: supply_risk_score has the same distribution across all end_use categories.
interpretation: Reject H0 (p=0.0000): average supply-risk score varies significantly across end-use categories in this dataset.

name: Pearson correlation test
hypothesis: H0: no linear association between market concentration (HHI) and supply_risk_score.
interpretation: Reject H0 (r=0.93, p<0.001): HHI and supply_risk_score exhibit a strong statistical association in this dataset -- expected, since the risk score is partly derived from concentration metrics. This is a statistical association, not a claim of independent causation.

name: Wilcoxon signed-rank test
hypothesis: H0: no systematic difference between 2015 and 2026 prices across minerals (paired).
interpretation: Reject H0 (p=0.0000): prices in 2026 are systematically different from 2015 across the mineral set.
